notes: Snapshot: Mid-market B2B SaaS (product analytics + in-app help). Initial adoption via Redwood Hosted API — good dev experience. Now evaluating Dedicated for predictability and cost. Short bullets: - Workloads: mix of chat-support (multi-turn), doc-search + embeddings for knowledge base, and reranking on search results. Peak traffic profile: daily spikes (10:00-12:00, 16:00-18:00 ET), expected 80-150 QPS during spikes. Targets: 95th pct latency for chat completions <220ms token time (end-to-end), avg latency for embeddings <60ms, error rate <1% under sustained load. - POC ask: provision Dedicated pool for 2-week canary: 2 GPU nodes (A100/4?) with traffic split 5% production->canary initially, ramp to 30% if stable. Validate canary+rollback runbook. - Routing/fallback plan: primary route to dedicated low-latency model variant (quantized 8-bit), fallback to hosted API variant in same region if Dedicated capacity exhausted, secondary failover to alternative region (us-west->us-east) with automated reroute, and last-resort degrade to smaller model with reduced context for latency guarantees. Need to exercise model variants (base fp16 -> q4_0 -> smaller family) and measure semantic regression. - Observability required: token-level cost, per-route 95p latency, KV cache hit rates, tracing for request path. Must be able to set automatic fallback thresholds (e.g., 95p latency >300ms or error rate >1%). - Security: SOC2 required, SSO/SAML for console, KMS for keys, audit logs retention 1 year, US data residency. - Success criteria (POC): sustained 95p latency <220ms at target load, error rate <1%, cost per 1M tokens within 30% of estimate, no customer data egress incidents. - Quote from CTO Ellen Park: 'If Redwood can prove predictable 95p latency and a clean canary/rollback story, we'll move to Dedicated commit Q2.' - Logistics: Legal needs DPA updates (work in progress); infra team needs list of egress IPs and VPC peering steps. Links: POC scope doc + security QA in Drive. Jira INFRA-1129 for peering rule request.
